verification_checks.method: read the borrowed bounded runner run_bounded()
verification_checks.detail: run_bounded creates the child itself and only ever calls terminate()/kill() on that own handle; it never enumerates or signals any other process. The per-process timeouts are enforced by a monotonic deadline inside the runner, and stdout+stderr are capped at 4 MiB. The receipt's owned_pids_only = true is a constant emitted by the tool rather than an observation, but the underlying behaviour is correct by construction.

minor.title: the terminal receipt reports a bogus start timestamp
minor.detail: prepare() stores started_at as datetime.fromtimestamp(started) where started is a time.monotonic() reading, so the recorded value is a 1970 epoch artefact (the receipt shows 1970-01-01T11:41:51.999572+00:00, which is the machine uptime at run start). The reproduction is recorded in raw/independent-verification-01.log section F.
minor.impact: an auditor cannot use started_at to place the run inside an authorised time window. No counter, budget, hash, decision or limitation is affected: wall_seconds_used is a correct monotonic delta and finished_at is a real wall-clock stamp.
minor.recommendation: derive started_at from time.time() or from a separately captured wall-clock value, and label the monotonic reading separately from the wall-clock reading.

minor.title: several cleanup and budget zeros are hard-coded constants rather than measurements
minor.detail: cleanup.owned_pids_only, cleanup.source_files_modified, cleanup.source_files_deleted and the budget zeros model_actions / gpu_actions / services / network_calls / downloads / full_product_checkpoints / browser_sessions are literal values assigned at construction, not values observed during the run. The underlying behaviour is correct (run_bounded only terminates the handle it created; the tool opens sources read-only and calls no model, network or download path), but the receipt presents these as if they had been observed.
minor.impact: the receipt is accurate in substance but overstates the strength of its own evidence for these particular fields. There is no complete OS-level audit in this run that could exclude every possible egress, and this review does not claim one.
minor.recommendation: mark these fields as policy declarations, or add an explicit instrumentation that counts them.

minor.title: the test suite's media-access audit hook covers less than its docstring claims
minor.detail: the suite patches builtins.open and os.scandir and asserts that nothing under the real media root was touched. Empirically verified in this review: the patch does not intercept io.open, pathlib.Path.open, os.open, os.stat or os.listdir. Pillow's own image reads do go through builtins.open and are therefore covered, which is the case that matters most, but the docstring's word 'prove' overstates the coverage.
minor.impact: the guarantee that the synthetic suite never reached the real 32 candidates is strong but not exhaustive. The separate guarantee that the real run touched exactly the frozen 32 candidates is independently supported by the committed command inventory and the candidate-level source hashes, which this review verified.
minor.recommendation: widen the hook to os.open and os.stat, or soften the docstring to state the exact interception set.

minor.title: the global wall deadline is not enforced inside a running decoder process
minor.detail: the 1200 s global budget is checked between candidates and during hashing, but a single ffprobe or ffmpeg call is bounded only by its own timeout (20 s and 45 s). A run could therefore overrun the global budget by up to about 45 s. The preflight check budget.global_deadline_governs acknowledges that the per-process timeouts can exceed the budget, but the point is not repeated in the receipt limitations list.
minor.impact: none in this run, which used 13.293 s of the 1200 s budget.
minor.recommendation: state the residual overrun in the limitations list.
